headline: Highest risk is data leakage: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and networked APIs while argo-workflows can move artifacts over REST/gRPC, creating a plausible shared-data path with limited isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct injection path is not documented, but OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP servers and stdin/stdout while argo-workflows can pass artifacts through APIs. If operators bridge them via copy-paste or a shared channel, content from one could be misread as instructions by the other. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above none.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected through copy-paste, stdin/stdout, or an MCP bridge
IF one agent parses the other's text artifacts as instructions
mitigations: Disable any text-based bridge between the agents
Require explicit provenance labels on all exchanged artifacts
Use a separate review step before executing instructions from either agent

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and can expose MCP/REST interfaces; argo-workflows handles artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted network egress. A shared workspace or API handoff could move sensitive financial content into outputs or logs. The pair is not proven to share storage, so this is medium rather than high, but the pathway exists in common deployments.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace, API payloads, or artifact store
IF financial or licensed data from OpenBBTerminal is included in artifacts consumed by argo-workflows
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials for each agent
Redact financial and licensed fields before handoff
Turn off artifact logging for sensitive payloads
Restrict network egress destinations to approved endpoints

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo-workflows has allowlisted egress and API-based orchestration, while OpenBBTerminal supports MCP/REST but has no filesystem write, shell, or git modification capability. There is some overlap on networked interfaces, yet the profiles do not show shared mutable writes or locking conflicts. That makes direct capability contention possible only in narrow orchestrations.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external API or datastore
IF an orchestrator routes concurrent updates without locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint API scopes per agent
Add optimistic-concurrency checks on shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can emit financial analyses through MCP/REST, and argo-workflows can consume artifacts and parameters in downstream workflows. If argo-workflows treats OpenBBTerminal output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into automated pipeline actions. The pair does not prove such automation by default, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF argo-workflows consumes OpenBBTerminal output without validation
IF downstream workflow steps act on those outputs automatically
mitigations: Insert a validation gate before workflow execution
Require human approval for high-impact downstream steps
Compare outputs against a second source before acting

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data, while argo-workflows handles artifacts and parameters with allowlisted egress. If regulated financial or licensed content is routed through argo-workflows into OpenBBTerminal outputs or logs, retention and residency obligations can be breached. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so uncertainty warrants the higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is processed by both agents
IF logs or artifacts are retained outside the required jurisdiction or retention policy
mitigations: Disable or shorten retention on shared logs and artifacts
Route sensitive data only through compliant storage
Review residency and DPA terms before deployment
